text.title: CLAUDE.md Creation — Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes of CLAUDE.md project briefs. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Stale commands: a script was renamed or removed and CLAUDE.md still tells the agent to run it, so every session opens with a failing command and an improvised replacement.
failure-mode.detector: Run each command in `## Commands` on a clean checkout; any non-zero exit. Diff the command names against `package.json` scripts, `Makefile` targets and `pyproject.toml` tooling.
failure-mode.repair: Regenerate the section with `templates/extract-commands.sh`, run every command once, and add the manifest-versus-CLAUDE.md check to CI so the next rename fails the build.

failure-mode.description: Secret pasted in: an `.env` block or a connection string with credentials was copied into the file "so the agent can run it", and is now in git history and every session's context.
failure-mode.detector: Secret scanner (gitleaks, trufflehog, host scanner) flags the file; regex for `://user:pass@`, `sk-`, `AKIA`, `-----BEGIN` hits.
failure-mode.repair: Rotate the credential, replace with `NAME=<required>` and a pointer to `.env.example`, rewrite history if policy requires, and add the scanner as a pre-commit hook on the file.

failure-mode.description: The novel: architecture history, coding philosophy and a copy of the README, well over the declared budget, paid on every turn of every session.
failure-mode.detector: Token count exceeds the template header's `token-budget-impact` by more than 20%; sections duplicate README or ADR content; prose paragraphs outnumber commands and paths.
failure-mode.repair: Cut to commands, structure, conventions, key files and gotchas; move narrative to linked files behind `@path` imports or one-line pointers; keep the budget line in the header true.

failure-mode.description: Tree dump: `## Structure` is a `tree -L 3` paste including `node_modules`, `dist` and `__pycache__`, with no purpose per entry.
failure-mode.detector: Structure section lists generated directories or has entries with no purpose phrase; entry count above roughly 20; paths that no longer exist.
failure-mode.repair: Keep only the paths a developer needs in the first hour, each with a one-phrase purpose; verify each path exists at commit time.

failure-mode.description: Generic gotchas: "write clean code", "add tests", "follow best practices" fill the section and drown the one line that would have saved a session.
failure-mode.detector: Gotcha entries that name no file, env var, command, version or lint rule.
failure-mode.repair: Delete generic entries; rewrite the survivors as trigger plus consequence with a concrete name ("`DATABASE_URL` has no default; the app exits at startup without it").

failure-mode.description: Personal paths committed: one developer's absolute venv path, local port or editor preference sits in the shared file and breaks for everyone else and for CI.
failure-mode.detector: Grep the committed file for `/Users/`, `/home/`, `C:\`, personal handles and non-default local ports.
failure-mode.repair: Move the lines to `CLAUDE.local.md` (kept out of version control) or `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; keep only what is true for every contributor in the project file.
